exposure: Nickel chloride hexahydrate (Ni) at doses of 46.125 mg/kg, 92.25 mg/kg, and 184 mg/kg body weight per day
outcome: Skeletal congenital abnormalities (incomplete ossification of skull bones, unossified interparietal bone, open arch of atlas, incomplete ossification of vertebrae, supernumerary lumbar rib, incomplete ossification of ribs and sternebrae, incomplete ossification of bones of forelimb, incomplete ossification of bones of hindlimb, unossified carpals, metacarpals, tarsals, metatarsals, and phalanges)
cohort: Forty pregnant female Balb/C albino mice and their embryos/fetuses were divided into a control group and three experimental groups.
finding: Nickel chloride hexahydrate exposure during the organogenetic period significantly decreased live-birth pups, increased resorption sites and stillbirth fetuses, and resulted in various skeletal congenital abnormalities in mice embryos.
gest_age: Exposure started from the 6th gestational day for 8 successive days, covering the organogenetic period, with fetuses examined after this period.
